subject: AcmeHealth: Private VPC data flow & privacy follow-up
messages:
From: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Singh <rajesh.singh@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro / Private VPC discussion follow-up

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — really helpful. Couple quick follow-ups from our side as we evaluate a Private VPC deployment:

- We need confirmation that PII can be prevented from leaving our VPC (no customer data persisted by Redwood).
- Data retention: what controls do you expose for token-level logs and how long are they retained by default?
- Logging & audit: can we get per-request audit logs and an option to ship logs to our SIEM?
- Network boundary: we need a diagram of how traffic flows between our VPC and Redwood control plane and whether there are any egress endpoints we need to open.

Looping in Rajesh (security) — he may have more technical questions. Can you share a short network/data flow diagram and any data handling docs?

Best,
Alice
Director of Product, AcmeHealth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rajesh Singh <rajesh.singh@acmehealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-01T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro / Private VPC discussion follow-up

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

Recap (answers in short):
- PII persistence: In Private (VPC) deployments, customer request payloads are not persisted by default outside customer-managed stores. We offer an option to disable any long-term token logging.
- Data retention: default ephemeral logs are 7 days for transaction traces in the runtime; configurable down to 0 days and up to 90 days for compliance needs.
- Audit logs: we can stream audit logs to your S3/CloudWatch/Splunk endpoint. We also provide request-level metadata in the logs (request id, model variant, route).
- Network flow: we will provide a network diagram — there is a small control-plane connection for billing/health to our control plane if you choose that mode; fully air-gapped on-prem options are also available.

Attachments: I attached a concise VPC network diagram and our data handling summary.

Next steps:
1) Neha (security) to confirm technical detail items and any additional questions.
2) Dev (solutions engineer) to propose an exact set of firewall rules/egress endpoints for your infra team.
3) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep dive with your network/security engineers (please propose times).

Would you prefer a fully air-gapped on-prem package or a VPC deployment with a control-plane link?

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: RDW_VPC_Network_Diagram.pdf (diagram stub), redwood-data-handling-summary.docx (summary stub)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rajesh Singh <rajesh.singh@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-01T20:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro / Private VPC discussion follow-up

Alice / team — thanks for the list, adding a few technical clarifications and questions from a security/compliance perspective:

1) Encryption: can you confirm whether customer payloads are encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest? For VPC we expect keys to be customer-managed (KMS/HSM) — is that supported?
2) Tokenization/PII handling: do you provide any built-in PII scrubbing or tokenization at the edge prior to sending requests to the runtime?
3) KV cache: if using context/cache features, how is the cache persisted and can it be disabled or stored on customer-managed storage?
4) Audit/export SLA: what is the delivery SLA for streamed audit logs to our SIEM?
5) Egress policy: please list all outbound IPs/hostnames required for the VPC connectors and any 3rd-party services.

For us to avoid surprises during procurement, a short matrix mapping controls -> available configuration (default behavior, configurable option, customer-managed option) would be ideal. I've attached a quick template we use for vendor evaluations — fill out the left column and we can return it with answers.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: vendor-security-template.xlsx (stub)

From: Rajesh Singh <rajesh.singh@acmehealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-02T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro / Private VPC discussion follow-up

Neha / Marissa — thanks for the quick responses. A few follow-ups from our infra team:

- If we choose VPC with control-plane link: which ports and FQDNs do we need to allow outbound? Can you provide IP ranges rather than FQDNs?
- On egress controls: we need to lock down egress so only the connector can talk out; does Redwood provide a managed connector appliance/container that initiates outbound to Redwood endpoints, or is it a customer-run agent?
- For the air-gapped option: what is the lifecycle for security patches and how do we apply runtime updates?

Also — please include any SOC2 attestations or penetration test reports you can share under an NDA.

Regards,
Rajesh
Head of Infrastructure, AcmeHealth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@acmehealth.com>, Rajesh Singh <rajesh.singh@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, legal@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-05-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro / Private VPC discussion follow-up

Rajesh / Alice — great questions. Quick answers and proposed deliverables by EOD Wednesday:

- Outbound endpoints: we will provide a minimal IP range list and FQDNs for the connector. For VPC with control plane link we recommend outbound on 443 to the following managed ranges (will provide exact CIDR blocks in deliverable).
- Connector model: we offer both a customer-run connector (lightweight container you deploy that brokers requests) and a managed connector option for Dedicated customers. The connector initiates outbound TLS to Redwood — you can lock egress to only that container.
- Air-gapped lifecycle: we provide an offline patch bundle and step-by-step upgrade runbook; updates are applied by your infra team. We also offer optional managed update assistance under our Private support package.
- KMS/HSM: supported for on-prem deployments; for VPC we support customer-managed KMS in your cloud account.
- Audit logs: default delivery SLA for streamed logs is 5 minutes; we can provide delivery guarantees in contract.
- SOC2 & pentest: happy to share under NDA — I'll loop in our compliance team via a secure link.

Deliverables we will send by EOD Wednesday:
1) IP/CIDR list + FQDN list for outbound (connector & control-plane).
2) Filled vendor-controls matrix (Neha to own final answers).
3) Updated VPC network diagram showing connector placement and egress lock-down.
4) Link to SOC2 report (NDA protected).

Please reply with a couple of 60-minute slots for a technical deep dive this week (we have availability Thursday 9–12 PT and Friday 10–3 PT).

Thanks — looking forward to the deep dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0124
